title: WCAG 2.2 keyboard focus visibility with sticky elements
statement:
WCAG 2.2 requires that a control receiving keyboard focus is not entirely hidden by author-created content such as sticky headers, cookie banners or chat widgets, so landing pages with fixed elements must keep the focused item visible when tabbing through the page.

Options:
- Scroll-padding offset: Sticky header with CSS scroll-padding-top equal to the header height so focused elements scroll clear of it (fits: modern, technical, polished)
- No sticky header: Static (non-sticky) header on long landing pages, with in-page anchor links for navigation (fits: minimal, calm, editorial)
- Compact sticky bar: Compact sticky bar kept as short as practical to reduce the area that can cover focused items, tested by tabbing forwards and backwards (fits: efficient, modern, conversion-focused)
- Dismissible banners: Cookie and consent banners that do not cover focusable content, or that the user can dismiss (for example with Esc) without moving focus (fits: respectful, trustworthy, careful)
- Bottom bar with offset: Bottom sticky CTA bar paired with matching scroll-padding-bottom (fits: mobile-first, conversion-focused, modern)
appliesWhen: Applies to: general web. Audience: general.
